source_description: A placard includes a visual image written with texts: “Education is Power”, “Resistance Never Futile” and “Read Banned Books”. Slices of watermelon symbolise the colours of the Palestinian flag (red, black, white, and green), representing Palestinian resistance against the Israeli occupation, particularly significant during the 1993 ban on the Palestinian flag. The black and white checkered keffiyeh print is also a symbol of the resilience of Palestinians. Three individuals depicted wearing keffiyehs are shown holding books in the visual imagery in sync with the message of reading banned books.

source_description: New Glyphs, New Writings by Another Graphic Typography is never neutral. This publication exposes it for what it truly is: a constructed system — shaped by tools, culture, technology, power, and politics. Structured in four parts, New Glyphs, New Writings unfolds through critical writing, experimental design, and typographic subversion. It questions how we design type, what systems we follow, and whose voices we amplify — or exclude. From rejecting industry-standard software to exploring ornamentation, script diversity, and the infrastructural politics of Unicode, the publication brings together a wide spectrum of perspectives — with contributions by Pentagram, Bye Bye Binary, Margot Lévêque, Morgane Vantorre, Charlotte Rohde, Clara Sambot, Laura Csocsán, Heikki Lotvonen, Rüdiger Schlömer, Lisa Huang, and more. But this isn’t just content — the form reflects the method. The publication consists of four parts: A large folder houses three smaller nested folders. Inside each: three A4 sheets printed recto verso, folded, cut, or restructured; a 12-page stapled booklet; a zigzag-folded infographic; and a double-sided A2 poster. All held together with a textile blue rubber band. The entire object is built on our visual identity system and typeset in Monotesk — modular, monospace, analytical. Every detail is intentional. Every constraint is embraced. Printed in full-color CMYK, featuring our Another Graphic Blue (Custom PMS!). Designed by Studio Studio. Edition of 500. Available…

For Another Graphic we developed a variable identity, based on the notion of an archive. Every component indicates an analysis of this term and reveals it in a tote bag. Another Graphic challenged designers to play with the system and the elements from the Another Graphic Visual Dynamic Identity. The winning design is by Ben Christensen, he designed this tote bag and we printed it. Cotton density: 140 g/m² Dimensions: 38 x 42 cm Capacity: 10l Ethically produced and chlorine free.
